name: Buck Euchre
description: Buck Euchre is a cutthroat (non-partnership) version of Euchre for 4-6 players. Each player plays entirely for themselves. Unlike standard Euchre's fixed 4-player partnerships, Buck Euchre is a standalone player-vs-all game. The dealer selects trump by flipping the top card of the kitty, and each player may order up or pass. The player who orders wins or loses alone based on how many tricks they take.
deck: 32 cards (Euchre deck: 9, 10, J, Q, K, A in 4 suits; 2-8 removed)

history.origins: Buck Euchre is an American variant of standard 4-player Euchre, adapted for larger groups where partnership play is impractical. It is particularly popular in the American Midwest.
timeline: 1800s: Standard Euchre firmly established in the American Midwest.
Late 1800s-1900s: Buck Euchre variants emerge for four players in Ohio and for three players in Indiana.
Present: Regional variant; popular in rural Midwest and other North American card nights.
history.cultural: A staple of American Midwest and broader North American card culture, often played at home games, community halls, and social gatherings where everyone plays for themselves.
history.evolution: By removing partnerships and making each player responsible for their own trump bid and tricks, Buck Euchre shifts the game from coordinated partnership play to individual risk management, closer to Rams-style penalty games.

setup.players: Four players, each for themselves; some groups extend to 5-6 players by adding extra low cards as described in Dirty Clubs variants.
setup.deck: 24 cards (A, K, Q, J, 10, 9 of each French suit) for the core four-player Buck Euchre game; groups that add players can extend the pack with extra low cards such as eights and sevens.
setup.dealing: 5 cards each. Remaining cards form a kitty; top card turned face-up to propose trump.

rules.objective: Score points by successfully making your trick bid, or lose points for failing.
rules.gameplay: Whoever orders up is the Maker and plays alone. Others try to prevent them from making their contract. Maker must win 3 of 5 tricks to succeed.
keyRules: Jacks of trump (Right Bower) and Jacks matching trump color (Left Bower) are the two highest trump cards.
Euchred = lose 2 points, regardless of how many tricks were taken.

strategy.basic: Only order up if you hold both Bowers or an Ace of the proposed trump suit plus at least 2 more trump cards.
strategy.intermediate: Void Strategy: Having a void suit allows you to trump early. In Buck Euchre, no one is helping youâ€”voids are both an asset (can trump) and a risk (others know your distribution).
strategy.advanced: Card counting across 4-6 players is difficult. Focus on knowing where the Right Bower is when you hold the Left Bowerâ€”bids with Left Bower only but no Right Bower are very risky.
tips: Going alone with both Bowers + Ace of trump is a near-certain March (5 tricks).
Watch the discard from the kittyâ€”it tells you what suit was rejected.

variations.name: Dirty Clubs
variations.description: Dirty Clubs is a related variant in which players bid for the right to name trumps (or no trumps), clubs can be called as trump even when not turned, and extra low cards are added when more than four players sit down.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Dirty Clubs rule differences are described in the source text; structured engine-level overrides for bidding and deck size are not yet encoded.
